jobs.occupation: Project Planning Specialist, Medium Voltage Products
jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

**This position reports to:

**Product Marketing Manager

__

**What we believe in:

**At ABB, we are dedicated to addressing global challenges head-on. Our core values: care, courage, curiosity, and collaboration - combined with a focus on diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunities - are important drivers in our goal to enable everyone to create sustainable solutions. This is our story. Make it your story.

**Role and tasks

**As Project Planning Specialist, you will combine project planning and control with operational sales administration support within ABB’s Medium Voltage Products business. Working closely with project managers and colleagues across sales administration, engineering, finance, procurement and operations, you will create reliable schedules, maintain accurate SAP data and provide clear insights into project costs, revenue, cash flow, risks and opportunities.

The role is designed with a broad scope. Alongside project planning responsibilities, you will support the sales administration team during peak workload periods and planned absences and help administer project-related financial guarantees. Your work will contribute to reliable project delivery, accurate commercial data and continuity in day-to-day operations. The position is based at our office in Middelfart and follows a hybrid work model.

• Maintaining and improving SAP master data, including material creation, sales item maintenance, product group structures and customer segmentation.

• Developing and maintaining integrated project schedules, including baselines, forecasts, milestones, resources and critical-path activities.

• Monitoring project progress, costs, revenue and cash flow, and providing regular reports and forecasts to the project team and relevant stakeholders.

• Identifying scheduling or cost deviations and working with project managers to define practical corrective actions.

• Creating, administering and maintaining advance payment guarantees, warranty guarantees and other project-related financial securities.

• Providing operational support and backup during peak workload periods and planned absences within the sales administration team.

• Supporting project risk, change, contract and claims management by assessing potential schedule and cost impacts and contributing to mitigation plans.

• Coordinating planning activities with engineering, procurement, finance, customers, contractors and other stakeholders while contributing to improvements in local tools and processes.

**Qualifications For The Role

**

• Hands-on experience using SAP for master data maintenance, material creation, sales item maintenance or related sales administration tasks.

• Experience with project planning, project control, project coordination or a related area.

• Ability to develop and maintain project schedules and analyze milestones, dependencies and critical paths.

• Experience monitoring project costs, forecasts, cash flow or other financial project information.

• Experience with financial guarantees, commercial administration or similar project-related documentation is helpful.

• Familiarity with project risks, changes, contracts or claims is helpful.

• A relevant educational background in engineering, finance, business, project management or another applicable field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Ability to organize information, manage parallel activities and communicate clearly in English; Danish proficiency is an advantage.

**More About Us

**At ABB, we have a clear goal of promoting diversity and inclusion in terms of gender, LGBTQ+, disability, ethnicity, and age. Together, we have embarked on a journey where we all individually and collectively celebrate and welcome individual differences. You can look forward to joining an organization that emphasizes employee well-being. Collaboration and team spirit are key words for us and a crucial foundation for reaching our shared goals. We prioritize a good working environment highly and continuously invest in the education and development of you and your colleagues. If you want to read more about our continuous work with the working environment and sustainability, you can find more information at: https://global.abb/group/en/sustainability

You will be based at our office in Middelfart, alongside team members and colleagues. In addition, we offer the possibility of working from home a few days a week.

The position reports to Product Marketing Director Morten Hellesøe.

Apply for the job online via our simple and easily accessible system, where you can also sign up to receive notifications on other opportunities within ABB. If you have questions about the position before then, you are welcome to contact Morten Hellesøe at +4540278387.

The application deadline is 11.11.2026. We look forward to receiving your application.

Project Director, Healthcare – Aarhus

Do you want to take ownership of one of the most strategic and visible programmes in Danish digital health? As Project Director, you will lead a comprehensive, product-strategic initiative for our electronic patient record (EPR) product, which has the potential to become the foundation for international growth. Sounds exciting? Then seize the chance now!

Systematic Healthcare – a coherent healthcare system

Systematics’ healthcare solutions are used by more than 200,000 users in, among others, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UK and New Zealand. Our EPR solution is the core system in a hospital and has been developed in close collaboration with our customers.

Experienced Project Director with ownership, impact and business understanding

As Project Director, you will have overall responsibility for one of Systematics’ most strategic initiatives: an extensive, long-term, product-strategic programme for our EPR product. The programme is closely linked to the EPR solution used in Western Denmark today and is characterised by high complexity, both internally and externally, with many stakeholders including our customers.

The role is not only about delivering on time, price, scope and quality - as our new Project Director, you help create the framework for the program and ensure that both our customers and Systematic realise the expected benefits.

You are the programme’s single point of accountability towards both the steering committee, our customers management and the management in Systematic.

The programme is run as a virtual organisation across tracks such as development, product management, customer projects, implementation and operations. You have no direct reports and therefore create results through influence, trust, clear direction and strong governance. You report to the Vice President for the area and work closely with our customers, Product Management and the leadership of the EPR area.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Owning the programme plan, budget and business case, and ensuring a coherent solution and the expected benefits over the programme’s lifetime.

• Establishing and driving the programme’s governance and acting as the programme’s primary representative towards customer and Systematic management, including preparing and presenting decision papers.

• Actively owning and protecting the scope: challenging new requirements, driving priorities and ensuring an effective change management process.

• Owning the roadmap, schedule, milestones, budget and resource plan, and ensuring proactive risk management with timely escalation to the steering committee.

• Ensuring delivery in accordance with the agreements and leading changes and negotiations together with our Sales and Legal teams and the Vice President.

• Managing a complex stakeholder landscape, internally and externally, including customers and their regional top management, political decision-makers, clinical leadership, partners and internal units, and ensuring that the product roadmap is aligned with the programme’s commitments.

• Building and leading the virtual programme organisation across tracks and departments by setting direction, removing obstacles and being an ambassador for culture and collaboration. At the same time, you support the organisational change that the programme entails

You will be based at our office in Aarhus and can expect customer meetings around Denmark. Your success is measured by whether the programme delivers within the agreed time, price, scope and quality, and whether the benefits of the business case are realised. An important success criterion is the trust of customers and management in the programme.

Your competencies and qualifications

We envision that you have 10–15 years of experience in programme and project management, several of them with large, complex IT programmes of similar complexity: multi-year, with several parallel tracks, many stakeholders and organisational interfaces. You hold a master’s degree, for example in engineering, IT or economics, and ideally a certification in programme management, such as PMI PgMP or Axelos MSP.

In addition, we expect that you:

• Have experience from the IT industry and with public customers, large public contracts and politically governed organisations. Experience from the healthcare sector is a significant advantage.

• Have been responsible for budget, business case and contractual commitments, including negotiating changes with customers.

• Have experience reporting to executive management and steering committees, leading in matrix or virtual organisations without formal line authority, and taking part in organisational change.

• Have a strong understanding of business and finance, as well as experience in contract and risk management.

• Speak Danish as your native language and are fluent in English.

As a person, you:

Take ownership: You act as the owner of the programme, not as an administrator of plans and reports, and you have the courage to say no and make difficult prioritisations.

Lead through influence: You create commitment and results without formal authority.

Have executive presence and political awareness: You are credible at executive level and communicate complex topics clearly and in a balanced way.

Are commercial and customer-minded: You balance customer value with Systematic’s interests and understand the importance of our customers’ work for patients and clinicians.

Are structured, proactive and resilient: You create overview, make decisions on an incomplete basis, and keep your energy and calm throughout a long, high-paced programme.

Are demanding and inclusive: You create an open and honest environment where people are heard and their work is recognised.

Do you want to help Arla shape the future of milk planning? Working with advanced forecasting, AI, and optimization, you'll assist in developing innovative solutions that predict future milk supply and optimize how milk is allocated across our global production network.

“In Supporting & Cross Functions within IT & Digital, we partner with Global Trading & Planning, Arla International, and Arla Foods Ingredients. You will become part of a strong and collaborative team working closely with business stakeholders to drive value creation, co-create digital roadmaps and ensure we realize the full value of our digital investments across Arla.__”, says IT Value Partner, Mikkel Nissen.

About the job

You will work with two central solutions supporting Global Planning One Milk Balance and One Intake. One Milk Balance is Arla’s internally developed planning system for balancing raw milk supply with the needs of our dairies. It ensures that incoming milk, fat, and by-products are allocated according to site capacities and business priorities. The solution runs on Azure and integrates with SAP IBP, One Intake, and Power BI.

One Intake is Arla’s next-generation milk intake forecasting solution. Built on Databricks, it uses modern time-series models to improve visibility into future milk supply by combining data science, farmer insights, and supply chain planning. More specifically, you will

• Develop forecasting and optimisation solutions using Python, SQL, Databricks, Azure, and MLOps.

• Support the operational performance of One Milk Balance and One Intake.

• Turn analytical insights into actionable Power BI reporting.

• Work closely with global planners to improve forecasting, planning, and decision-making.

• A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics or a related field.

• At least two years of experience as a Data Scientist or in a similar technical role.

jobs.description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. You will own the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across infrastructure, network, and workforce identity security, and rolling out the first paved roads for a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen), workforce identity and access, and drift checks for cloud configuration and network rules. You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers, and every Veo employee, work securely across our offices and clouds.

**What You Will Do

**You'll join the Security Enablement Team and focus on the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership of the team's work, pair on complex problems, and rotate responsibilities. The systems themselves stay with the owning teams, and our job is to make those teams successful.

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for our office and data center networks and the VPN that connects them, as part of the network security direction the team sets together. Day-to-day operation and firewall changes stay with the team that owns the network

• Build patterns and tooling for secure cross-site connectivity and endpoint security posture that IT can adopt and run, in a way that supports how Veo engineers actually work

• Build the patterns and automation for workforce identity and access, including SSO hygiene, MFA enforcement for employees, and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows for access to product systems, with IT owning the day-to-day operation

• Build automated checks that surface drift in cloud configuration and network rules, so the owning teams get a signal and can act on it

• Act on infrastructure and network findings from external penetration tests, routed through the team's shared intake, with the owning teams driving remediation

• Build the first version of cross-cutting capabilities, such as the cross-site VPN or the drift checks, then hand each one to a long-term owner with a written transition that covers the runbook, ownership, and escalation path

• Partner with GRC to build evidence pipelines for IT and access-related controls that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Run office hours where IT, platform, and product teams can get a network or access review

As the team matures, you'll help shape how Veo's network and identity stack evolves across our offices and clouds as the company grows.

**What You Could Bring

**This role deliberately sits where IT, cloud, and security meet. You do not need to be world class at all three. You are strong in one or two and comfortable operating across the rest.

You likely have several years of experience at that intersection. That tends to show up in several of the following:

• Solid IT fundamentals: networking, identity, endpoint posture, MFA, and SSO at production scale

• Cloud infrastructure experience: hands-on work on at least one of GCP or AWS, including IAM, networking, and basic Terraform-style IaC

• Workforce identity and access: hands-on experience with SSO and identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace) and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows

• A security mindset layered on that IT and cloud depth: you instinctively look for misconfigurations, drift, and bad access patterns, without needing to be a dedicated security specialist

• Cross-context comfort: you can work on an office network problem and a product cloud problem in the same week without context-switching pain

• Platform-as-product mindset: you've built internal tooling that real teams adopt, with guard rails built into the tools people already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured impact

• Comfort handing work back to a long-term owner once the build phase is done

• Collaboration: you work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively, and write things down.

Nice to have: VPN solutions at scale (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, WireGuard), endpoint management tooling, and audit log pipelines.

**How We Work

**You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on most of it but not all of it, apply anyway. People who span IT, cloud, and security are rare, and we do not expect every box ticked. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for a position in which you can set direction and help shape our company? If so, then you could be the newest addition to our team as

**Senior Frontend Engineer – Tracking.

****Be part of the movement - and play your part.

****About The Role

**As a Senior Frontend Engineer – Tracking at DFDS, you will join a collaborative team working at the intersection of frontend engineering, customer data, analytics, and marketing technology. This is a role for someone who enjoys both hands-on implementation and seeing the bigger picture: how platforms, tracking, data flows, consent, and customer experiences connect to create better and more personalised journeys.

You will play an important part in strengthening our Martech foundation and helping us build more scalable and data-driven customer experiences across our digital platforms. **On a Day-to-day Basis, You Will

“We’re looking for someone who enjoys solving problems together, can see the bigger picture across customer data and platforms, and still loves getting hands-on with implementation.”

**About You

Working at DFDS At DFDS, you will be part of an environment where technology, collaboration, and business impact go hand in hand. This role offers the opportunity to work on meaningful digital initiatives that influence how we engage with customers across channels and platforms.

• Meaningful scope: Help shape the Martech and customer data foundation behind important digital journeys.

While you’re with us, we want you to develop. At DFDS, we believe that development happens first and foremost through activities in the workplace. We will also offer training courses that can support you in your role, if needed.

Are we a match? Then what are you waiting for? Apply Now. If you think your personality, skills, experience, and desire match this role, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your CV as soon as possible, as we’re keen to meet potential candidates on an ongoing basis.

jobs.description:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
  

  The position

  This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

   

  Project description

  The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

   

  Description of the scientific environment

  The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

   

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.
  

  The PhD programme

  You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.    

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is November 22, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk  

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.
